item.title: SonicWall patches actively exploited SonicOS VPN MFA bypass vulnerability CVE-2026-19868 added to CISA KEV
item.description:
Perimeter network security advisories published today confirm active wild exploitation targeting enterprise firewall SSL VPN gateways. Unauthenticated remote adversaries exploit single sign-on logic flaws to bypass SAML multi-factor authentication controls and establish persistent network footholds.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-19868 and added to the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog under Binding Operational Directive 26-04, impacts SonicOS running on SonicWall Gen7 and Gen8 firewall appliances. Remote threat actors holding credentials for alternate login methods send malformed SAML authentication assertions to bypass enforced multi-factor authentication checks, obtaining unauthorized remote access to corporate network perimeters. SonicWall released emergency firmware updates for versions 7.3.4-7013 and 8.2.3-8015, stating no administrative workarounds are available.
Subverting secure remote access controllers destroys perimeter network boundaries across enterprise environments. Because SonicWall firewalls manage corporate SSL VPN access and site-to-site IPsec tunnels, an unauthenticated SAML authentication bypass permits threat actors to hijack user sessions, inspect internal network transit traffic, and move laterally across production subnets.
- Upgrade SonicOS firmware installations immediately across Gen7 and Gen8 firewalls to maintenance builds 7.3.4-7013 or 8.2.3-8015. - Audit SAML identity provider configuration logs for anomalous single sign-on authentication assertions originating from unverified IP ranges. - Restrict public internet access to firewall management interfaces, placing administrative portals on isolated out-of-band VLANs. - Invalidate active remote access user session tokens and execute mandatory credential rotations across VPN user accounts.
Perimeter firewall controller defense demands immediate firmware patch application and rigid identity provider verification to ensure corporate remote access gateways remain insulated from authentication bypass exploits. #CodeDefence #SonicWall #SonicOS #MFA #SAML #AuthBypass #CISA #KEV #NetworkSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement

item.title: OpenSSH SSHole flaw CVE-2026-123158 targeted in wild honeypot root exploitation attempts
item.description:
Enterprise server infrastructure alerts issued today report automated scanning arrays targeting remote access authentication handlers within hours of public disclosure. Threat actors exploit authentication parsing logic errors to log into passwordless system accounts without presenting credentials.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-123158 carrying a CVSS score of 8.1 and codenamed SSHole, impacts Linux environments running OpenSSH compiled against the musl C library with Pluggable Authentication Modules PAM disabled. Unauthenticated remote adversaries transmit crafted SSH authentication packets to bypass empty password verification subroutines, achieving instant remote shell access under root privileges on exposed hosts. Threat intelligence sensors detected automated exploitation attempts hitting public honeypots within hours of technical details circulating online.
Subverting secure shell authentication daemons presents immediate systemic risks to Linux server fleets, cloud container nodes, and embedded infrastructure. Because OpenSSH provides primary administrative access to Linux servers, an unauthenticated SSH authentication bypass allows threat actors to establish persistent root backdoors, harvest system secrets, and exfiltrate host data.
- Force immediate patch installation for OpenSSH packages across all Linux distributions and cloud container images. - Re-enable Pluggable Authentication Modules PAM or migrate OpenSSH installations to glibc-backed release builds. - Enforce public-key authentication exclusively, disabling password authentication and root login across sshd_config files. - Restrict inbound SSH port 22 access using strict firewall rules, zero trust access proxies, or bastions.
Secure shell infrastructure security demands immediate package updating and zero trust network isolation to ensure enterprise Linux hosts remain protected against unauthenticated authentication bypass exploits. #CodeDefence #OpenSSH #SSHole #Linux #AuthBypass #RCE #ServerSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement #ThreatIntelligence

item.title: Claude Code persistent settings file exposes developer passwords and API keys across 1122 public GitHub repositories
item.description:
Developer security research writeups published today reveal widespread credential exposure stemming from automated AI coding assistant configuration files. Plaintext passwords, API tokens, and secret keys typed by developers into terminal commands were committed to public code repositories.
The security finding involves Anthropic Claude Code command persistence mechanisms. When developers execute terminal commands through Claude Code and select the Don't Ask Again prompt confirmation, the AI assistant saves the full executed command string, including plaintext passwords, database connection credentials, and API access keys, into local project settings files. Developers subsequently committing project folders to public GitHub repositories accidentally exposed 1,122 public configuration files containing live infrastructure credentials.
Exposing corporate credentials and infrastructure secrets within public code repositories introduces severe software supply chain and cloud environment exposure. When secret tokens land on public code repositories, automated credential harvesting bots extract keys within seconds, allowing threat actors to hijack cloud hosting accounts, access private databases, and compromise software release pipelines.
- Add Claude Code local configuration settings files to global .gitignore files across all developer workstations immediately. - Scan corporate GitHub repositories and organization commits for exposed project configuration files containing plaintext secrets. - Execute immediate credential revocations and token rotations for all passwords, API keys, and access tokens committed to repositories. - Enforce automated pre-commit secret scanning hooks across developer workstations to block commits containing sensitive strings.
Developer environment governance requires rigid secret scanning and continuous credential rotation to ensure AI coding tools do not inadvertently leak corporate infrastructure credentials into public code repositories. #CodeDefence #Anthropic #ClaudeCode #GitHub #SecretLeak #CredentialTheft #DevSecOps #AppSec #SupplyChain #IdentitySecurity
